idiom_name: Map or WeakMap pool plus Object.freeze; primitives are already shared values
implementation_notes: JavaScript primitives already behave like flyweights - strings and numbers are immutable values, engines deduplicate literals, and equality is by value - so the pattern collapses into local idioms instead of a class hierarchy: a Map (or a WeakMap for object keys) as the factory pool, Object.freeze or immutable updates so the shared object cannot be written, and the extrinsic state as ordinary per-object fields. Sharing methods through the prototype chain (Object.create(shared)) is the same trick applied to behaviour. Reach for the explicit factory when the pooled state is expensive to build or when reference equality (===) is used as the equality test, as in renderers and caches.
pitfalls: A long-lived Map is a strong reference: with unbounded keys the pool leaks. WeakMap is the fix when the key is an object, but primitives such as strings cannot be weak keys, so bounded key sets still need eviction.
Object.freeze is shallow: a frozen flyweight holding an array or nested object remains mutable through the inner reference; freeze deeply or expose only primitives.
Keys built with template literals allocate on every lookup, which can cost more than the deduplication saves in hot loops; cache the key or nest Maps by field.
Objects shared through the prototype chain are not own properties, so Object.keys, JSON.stringify and spread ignore the shared state - a frequent source of surprise.
